details.description: FLUX.1 [dev] FP8 is Fireworks AI's FP8 (8-bit floating point) quantized serving build of Black Forest Labs' FLUX.1 [dev], a 12 billion parameter rectified flow transformer that generates images from text descriptions. The underlying model is the same open-weight, guidance-distilled model described by Black Forest Labs as offering output quality "second only to" its closed FLUX.1 [pro] model, and released under the FLUX.1 [dev] Non-Commercial License. As of September 2026, Fireworks' page for this specific fp8 build returns not-found, but an archived capture of it (2025-07-31) describes the build as using reduced-precision numerics for roughly 2x faster inference than the standard build, deployed via Fireworks' "Flumina" server-app toolkit; Black Forest Labs' current models listing is centered on the newer FLUX.2/FLUX 3 families rather than FLUX.1 [dev].
advantages: Black Forest Labs describes the underlying FLUX.1 [dev] model as offering "competitive prompt following, matching the performance of closed source alternatives".
Trained with guidance distillation, which the model card states makes FLUX.1 [dev] more efficient than a non-distilled equivalent.
Fireworks' archived page for this build states it uses reduced-precision (FP8) numerics for roughly 2x faster inference than the full-precision build.
Unlike the base FLUX.1 [dev] listing, Fireworks' archived page shows this FP8 build offered as both a serverless, pay-per-token deployment and an on-demand dedicated-GPU deployment.
disadvantages: Licensed under the FLUX.1 [dev] Non-Commercial License, which restricts commercial use without a separate agreement.
Fireworks lists fine-tuning, image input, and embeddings as not supported for the base FLUX.1 [dev] model this build derives from.
The base FLUX.1 [dev] model does not appear on Black Forest Labs' current models listing, which as of September 2026 is centered on the newer FLUX.2 and FLUX 3 generations.
use_cases: Generating images from text prompts for non-commercial or locally licensed use
Prompts that include rendered text, per the base model card's example prompts

notes: The live Fireworks page for this fp8 build, https://fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/flux-1-dev-fp8 (and the app.fireworks.ai equivalent), currently returns not-found. A prior pass could only confirm via the Wayback availability API that a 2026-05-17 snapshot had existed, without being able to read its content. On re-checking, the Wayback CDX API lists many working (HTTP 200) captures from 2025-04 through 2026-05, and I was able to fetch one directly (2025-07-31): it describes this build as using 'reduced precision numerics for 2x faster inference', deployed as a Fireworks 'Flumina' server app, and links to https://huggingface.co/fireworks-ai/FLUX.1-dev-fp8-flumina for more detail (that Hugging Face repo returns HTTP 401, consistent with a gated repo behind the FLUX.1 [dev] non-commercial license, so I could not read it directly). The same archived page's info panel shows 'Serverless: Available' and an 'On-demand Deployment' option, unlike the base (non-fp8) FLUX.1 [dev] listing, which lists serverless as not supported; the disadvantages list has been corrected to not imply the fp8 build itself lacks serverless. Also flag: sibling catalog entries flux-1-dev and flux-1-schnell (same provider) are tagged kind 'chat' with a /v1/chat/completions endpoint, while this fp8 entry is correctly tagged kind 'image' with /v1/images/generations - consistent with all of these being image-generation models and the 'chat' tagging on the non-fp8 siblings being the likely data anomaly.
